correctness.rationale: The known integral homology concentration in dimension four (Scoville arxiv:2604.18172v1, Table 2/Theorem 20) makes the ordinary Lefschetz number equal to 1+the H4 trace. The attached exhaustive finite procedure enumerates all 14,720 nonempty Hasse matchings exactly once, checks acyclicity over the entire directed face poset, and obtains 12,820 admissible simplices with exactly the published face vector. It evaluates oriented setwise-fixed-simplex traces and independently re-enumerates complete edge-orbit unions; both agree on each conjugacy class, with all 24 permutations checked. The exact irreducible character table and class sizes then give multiplicities (4,13,8,12,4). This is an exhaustive proof for one finite complex, not extrapolation.

value.rationale: The full three-simplex is the natural first higher-dimensional simplex where a large ordinary Morse matching complex has recently been classified as a 99-sphere wedge. The natural S4 action on its only nonzero reduced homology is a complete intrinsic representation invariant not determined by the published Betti number or automorphism group: five cycle-class traces reveal all five irreducible multiplicities and the distinction between standard and sign-twisted standard components. This exact natural benchmark is relevant to symmetry-sensitive discrete Morse theory despite not implying an all-simplex theorem.
